newsitem.title: USA: Norand denies Kensington lawsuit claims.
newsitem.headline: Norand denies Kensington lawsuit claims.

text.p: Norand Corp, which merged with Western Atlas Inc this week, Thursday denied allegations contained in a lawsuit filed by Kensington Electronics Inc over a contract both sides say was terminated in August.
In a lawsuit filed in an Orange County (California) Superior Court in December, Kensington alleged that Norand failed to pay $300,000 for residual inventory and related costs.
"We are aware of the litigation. We deny the claims and we will defend ourselves vigorously," Jim Johnson, Norand's corporate counsel, told Reuters.
"It was a contract matter, a complex agreement, that was terminated," Johnson said.

However, John Patrick Rabbitt of Aliso Viejo, California-based Kensington, said his company had no problem with the 18-month contract being terminated after 16 months. Kensington filed the suit because Norand was not living up to certain provisions in the pact, Rabbit alleged.
"The contract called for Norand to be responsible for any residual products made," Rabbitt said. "There were about $250,000 worth (of circuit boards left over) after the contract was cancelled."
Rabbitt said talks on settling the issue began about four months ago, adding that Norand offered about half of the amount allegedly owed as late as last week.
Norand spokesman Johnson declined to comment on any aspect of a possible settlement.
Kensington is a distributor of electronic components.
Norand makes mobile computing systems and wireless communications networks. Its shares closed unchanged Thursday at 33-1/8.
